# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1344._

> ℹ️ **11 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/common/tcTriage.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI red — crap ratchet fails (15 new functions over threshold 8), worst offender is dead code**

The `crap` check failed on head `056b9cea` (`ci_failures.md`, log line `0 regression(s), 15 new over threshold, 8 improvement(s)... exit code 2`), so the merge gate is red. The single worst offender is this function:

```
sameBuildAndEnv    js/common/tcTriage.js    CC 8    Cov 0.0%    CRAP 72.0
```

`sameBuildAndEnv` is **never called anywhere** — not by `triageValidatedGuard` (which uses `sameBuild` + `envChanged` directly), not by any caller, not by any test (`grep -rn sameBuildAndEnv` finds only its definition and export). Deleting it removes the 72-CRAP entry entirely.

The remaining 14 over-threshold functions need decomposition before the ratchet passes (new functions must land ≤ 8):

- `js/postStoryTestAutomationResults.js`: `triageBugFailures` (19.5), `entryRoleMeta` (17.1), `handleBugWithProductFailure` (16.1), `currentBuildSha` (10.4)
- `js/common/tcMaintenanceLedger.js`: `normalizeFinding` (17), `findingFromVerdict` (16), `findingFromDevClaim` (11), `findingLine` (11.2)
- `js/common/tcRunRegistry.js`: `recordGreen` (16), `recordFailure` (14)
- `js/common/tcTriage.js`: `pickEvidence` (14), `resolveTcRole` (10)
- `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`: `completeTestSuspectedPath` (12.2)
- `js/unit-tests/test_postStoryTestAutomationResults.js`: `triageModule` (9)

Concrete refactor guidance: extract per-entry step helpers (`triageBugFailures` → one-entry function), table-drive `pickEvidence`/`normalizeFinding` field copying with a `[key, sourceKeys]` loop, split `recordGreen`/`recordFailure` entry construction into a shared `mergeEntryState` helper, and split `entryRoleMeta` source selection into a small resolver chain. All are pure functions — the existing 51 new unit tests keep passing through mechanical extraction.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/tcMaintenanceLedger.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: dead code — `bits` is built and never used**

In `findingLine` (tcMaintenanceLedger.js:349-352) the `bits` array is populated with three conditional pushes and then discarded — the `return` statement below builds its own string from `f.tcKey`/`f.errorClass`/`f.testPath`/`f.occurrences` directly. The `bits` block is dead code that inflates complexity (the CRAP report flags `findingLine` at 11.2) and misleads readers into thinking it formats the output.

Delete the `bits` block (or, if the multi-part line was intended, actually render from `bits.join(' — ')` — but then the `dev claim`/`claimedVerdict` suffixes must move into it too, since today a dev finding renders its testPath twice-shaped: once via `bits` (dropped) and once via the return string).

---

### Thread 3 — `js/postStoryTestAutomationResults.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the bounce comment lists every TC twice**

`bugReturnComment` builds its own list under the header "The following Test Cases failed with a product regression:" (postStoryTestAutomationResults.js:744-745) and then appends `tcTriage.buildBounceComment(bouncedVerdicts)` — which opens with the **identical header and repeats the same TC list** (tcTriage.js:303-306). The posted comment therefore contains the same header + list twice back-to-back, only differing in the evidence suffix.

Render one list: either keep the legacy `failureList` and pass the verdicts only for the attribution paragraph, or drop the local list and let `buildBounceComment` (which already carries `failureSummary` per TC) own the section. A regression test asserting the TC key appears exactly once in the comment would pin this.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/postStoryTestAutomationResults.js` line 1094

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: in a mixed bounce+route run, routed findings are never staged or digested**

When `triage.bounced.length > 0` the function returns immediately after finalizing the bounced TCs — the `stageRoutedBugTestCases(triage.routed, ...)` call and the triage-digest `postComment` below it never run. A run that produces one earned bounce *and* (say) an environment-shifted guard leaves the routed TC at its previous status and its finding visible only inside the machine marker — no human-visible digest, inconsistent with the non-bounce path where the same verdict stages the TC and posts the digest. `escalated` verdicts are likewise reported in the result payload but never staged on either path.

Fix: before the bounce branch, stage routed TCs and append the triage/escalation digest sections to the bounce comment (or post the digest regardless of route), so every attributed finding gets the same human surface on every route.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/common/tcTriage.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: same-build red with missing env fingerprints is auto-classified "flaky" — contradicts the module's own evidence doctrine**

`triageValidatedGuard` treats a same-SHA red as `'flaky-same-build'` whenever `envChanged()` is false — including the case where **neither side has an env fingerprint** (the agent omitted `envFingerprint`, cf. the instruction "when you can identify the environment... record it"). Yet this module's own docstring for `sameBuildAndEnv` states: *"A missing half on either side never proves sameness — the comparison is evidence, not a default."* The live triage path does exactly what the doctrine forbids, defaulting an unproven case to "flaky" and routing it to maintenance.

Please confirm the intended reading. Options: route missing-fingerprint same-build reds to the `'rerun-requested-on-last-green-build'`/unknown-env reason instead of asserting `flaky-same-build`, or require both fingerprints before the flaky/environment-shift classification (falling through to the differential request otherwise). If "flaky by default" is deliberate, document it at the branch so the doctrine comment stops contradicting the code.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/common/tcTriage.js` line 294

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: legacy bounce path is now gated on agent-supplied `acVerdict` — confirm the degradation is intended**

`triageAcGated` bounces a validated own-oracle TC **only** when `acVerdict === 'violated'`; without an AC verdict it routes to `'own-oracle-ac-recheck'` (rework), and the run returns `status: 'test_maintenance'` with the bug untouched. Previously any red linked TC bounced the bug. So a bug run whose result entries lack the new metadata — an agent run that ignores the updated prompt contract, a hand-crafted or older-format `story_test_automation_result.json`, or a consuming repo that pins this submodule without updating its automation agent — will never bounce: every red degrades to rework/maintenance and the bug stalls in In Testing (the only exit being the redRounds escalation, which itself only fires via the `redRounds` registry streak).

The PR description claims "bounded legacy bounce path preserved" — in shape yes, but only when the agent actually emits `acVerdict`. Please confirm this fail-safe degradation is the accepted default for non-compliant results, and consider a tracker-comment hint when a failed own-oracle entry carries **none** of the new fields (`acVerdict`, `retryStatus`, `errorClass` all absent), so a stalled bug is diagnosable as "agent didn't follow the schema" rather than "product didn't regress".

---

### Thread 7 — `js/postStoryTestAutomationResults.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the bounce gate trusts the agent-copied `role`/`verifies` over the linked TC's own metadata**

`entryRoleMeta` returns the **result entry first**: if the automation agent supplied `role`/`verifies` (which the updated schema now instructs it to do on every failed entry), the linked TC's own metadata (`linkedEntry`, `linkedEntry.fields`) is never consulted. The entire scoping decision of gh-1329 — own oracle vs sibling vs guard, i.e. whether a TC may ever bounce the bug — thus rests on an LM-copied string. A hallucinated `verifies: "BUG-2"` silently demotes the bug's own acceptance oracle to `ROLE_SIBLING`, which by design can never bounce — the failure mode is invisible (no warning, verdict looks perfectly ordinary).

Since the TC description stamping is mechanical-truth-in-progress (declared guidance-only in the PR concerns), consider at least: (a) preferring `linkedEntry`/`fields` metadata when present (the TC ticket is the durable record; the result file is per-run), and (b) logging a warning when the entry's `verifies` disagrees with a linked-TC-provided value, so a mis-scoped oracle leaves a trace instead of silently demoting the gate.

---

### Thread 8 — `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
💡 **SUGGESTION: silent catches + duplicated bookkeeping plumbing in `completeTestSuspectedPath`**

Two issues in one place:

1. `try { tracker.postComment(ticketKey, ...); } catch (e) {}` (twice, developBugAndCreatePR.js:668-672) swallows failures with no log. The sibling implementation in this same PR (`postMarkerIfChanged`) logs `console.warn('Failed to post', label, 'marker (non-fatal):', e)` — a silently-dropped ledger marker means the next run rebuilds from the stale ledger and the finding's `occurrences` history drifts with nothing in the logs to explain it. Log the warnings.
2. The comment-fetching IIFE and the `machineAuthorOptsOf` construction duplicate `bugTrackedComments`/`machineAuthorOptsOf` in postStoryTestAutomationResults.js (and call `tracker.getIssue(ticketKey)` twice — once for the truthiness check, once for `.fields`). Extract one shared "load bug bookkeeping (comments + author opts)" helper into a common module and call it from both legs.

---

### Thread 9 — `js/postStoryTestAutomationResults.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `currentBuildSha` shells out once per result entry**

Both call sites in `triageBugFailures` (failed branch line 880, green branch line 918) invoke `currentBuildSha(result, entry, ctx.workingDir)`, which falls through to `runInRepo('git rev-parse HEAD', ...)` whenever the entry/result don't carry a SHA. For a bug with N linked TCs that is up to N identical subprocess invocations per run. Resolve the build SHA once per run (a `var buildSha = currentBuildSha(result, null, ctx.workingDir)` before the `forEach`) and pass it into both branches — the per-entry override (`entry.sha`) can still win inside the helper.

---

### Thread 10 — `js/common/tcMaintenanceLedger.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-11-03):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `note` duplicates `reason` for automation-sourced findings**

`normalizeFinding` sets both `reason: src.reason || null` and `note: truncate(firstDefined(src, ['note', 'reason']))` (tcMaintenanceLedger.js:124). # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything

- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

So a bug run whose result entries lack the new metadata — an agent run that ignores the updated prompt contract, a hand-crafted or older-format `story_test_automation_result.json`, or a consuming repo that pins this submodule without updating its automation agent — will never bounce: every red degrades to rework/maintenance and the bug stalls in In Testing (the only exit being the redRounds escalation, which itself only fires via the `redRounds` registry streak).

The PR description claims "bounded legacy bounce path preserved" — in shape yes, but only when the agent actually emits `acVerdict`. Please confirm this fail-safe degradation is the accepted default for non-compliant results, and consider a tracker-comment hint when a failed own-oracle entry carries **none** of the new fields (`acVerdict`, `retryStatus`, `errorClass` all absent), so a stalled bug is diagnosable as "agent didn't follow the schema" rather than "product didn't regress".

`entryRoleMeta` returns the **result entry first**: if the automation agent supplied `role`/`verifies` (which the updated schema now instructs it to do on every failed entry), the linked TC's own metadata (`linkedEntry`, `linkedEntry.fields`) is never consulted. The entire scoping decision of gh-1329 — own oracle vs sibling vs guard, i.e. whether a TC may ever bounce the bug — thus rests on an LM-copied string. 1:# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
2-#
3-# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
4-# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
5-# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
6-#

11-# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
12-#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
13-#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
14-# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
15-#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
16:#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
17-#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
18-#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
19-# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.

content.text:
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Duplication gate (production JS duplicated lines <= 1%, ratcheted)
        # Ratchet, not an absolute bar: a pinned set of production JS files
        # already exceeds 1% duplicated lines — pre-existing debt owned by the
        # gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets (see duplication-baseline.json for the
        # current pinned set) — so the measurement's exit 2 is expected for
        # now. The baseline pins each over-threshold file with its measured
        # percentage and absolute duplicated-line count; the gate FAILS only
        # on a NEW over-threshold file or a pinned file that gained ABSOLUTE
        # duplicated lines (ci/duplicationRatchet.js) — a percentage shift
        # caused by file shrinkage passes and is logged as informational —
        # keeping the absolute 1% bar as the end state once the debt lands.
        # A crashed measurement (tool exit other than 0/2) never passes.
        # js/unit-tests/** stays excluded; the badge step below reparses the
        # same measurement for the README endpoint.
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e
          node ci/duplicationRatchet.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" duplication-baseline.json "$code"

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"

content.text:
/**
 * findingRegistry.js — the finding-identity registry: deduplication of
 * review findings across review rounds (gh-1332).
 *
 * Live pathology (audit repro `s1c`): review rounds are stateless — round 1
 * raised 7 findings (REQUEST_CHANGES), the fix was reverted, and round 2
 * re-raised all 7 as brand-new. A naive matcher over path + line + claim
 * text found 0 duplicates: paraphrase ("nothing validates a token" ->
 * "sessions never expire") and line drift defeat any location- or
 * wording-based match. Each lap cost a full review leg and multiplied
 * duplicate threads; the machine could not tell a converging review from a
 * churning one.
 *
 * The protocol (all of it mechanical — creating/advancing the registry costs
 * the reviewer nothing beyond one-word candidate confirmations):
 *
 *   Identity    id = hash(file path + normalized behavior claim + severity
 *               class). NOT the line number (it drifts) and NOT the priority
 *               alone (too coarse). The claim is normalized (case,
 *               whitespace, punctuation) and its content words (stopwords
 *               dropped, light suffix stemming) drive similarity scoring.
 *
 *   Matching    Two stages — the machine proposes, the reviewer disposes.
 *               A false split (duplicate thread) is cheap; a false merge
 *               (masked defect) ships a bug, so the default is always NEW:
 *                 1. propose (mechanical): each new finding is compared
 *                    against OPEN registry items (same file + claim
 *                    similarity + severity class). Near-identical claims
 *                    auto-merge (surfaced); partial similarity becomes a
 *                    candidate ("possibly same as F3 — confirm or new"); no
 *                    candidate means unconditionally new.
 *                 2. confirm (reviewer, one word per candidate): "same as
 *                    F3" or "new". Unconfirmed candidates are NEW.
 *               Splits after the fact are the promoted/withdrawn lifecycle.
 *
 *   Lifecycle   open -> fixed (fixing hunk cited)     | resolved identities
 *               open -> withdrawn (reason REQUIRED)   | LEAVE the dedup
 *               open -> re-introduced (re-raise case) | space: candidates
 *               are drawn only from OPEN items, so a new finding at a
 *               resolved location is independent even in the worst matching
...
        'a genuinely new finding on a resolved item is expected to be raised again with new evidence.');
    return lines.join('\n');
}

**Status: fixed** — the bounce path no longer returns early past the routed findings.

- `bouncePathResult` (`js/postStoryTestAutomationResults.js:1160`) now: finalizes the bounced TCs → posts the bounce comment → **`stageRoutedBugTestCases(routedAndEscalated(triage), …)`** → **`postTriageDigest(triage, ctx)`** — the same staging + digest the non-bounce path performs.
- `escalated` verdicts are staged and digested on **both** paths via the same `routedAndEscalated` helper (`routed.concat(escalated)`), so they no longer only ride the result payload.
- `digestSections` composes the human surface identically on every route: triage digest (routed), escalation comment (escalated), the gh-1329 schema-gap hint (when a failed own-oracle entry carried none of the triage fields), and the TC-maintenance-ledger digest.

# Thread 6 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: legacy bounce path is now gated on agent-supplied `acVerdict` — confirm the degradation is intended

**Confirmed intended, and the suggested diagnosability hint is implemented.**

1. **The fail-safe default is the design, not an accident.** gh-1329's premise is that a red TC has four causes and a bounce must be *earned* (§3: rework first; bounce only on a confirmed AC violation; §2: a fresh TC cannot bounce by construction). With no `acVerdict` there is no confirmation — so the failure routes to rework/maintenance and the bug's state stays put. Bouncing on unattributable evidence would reintroduce the exact loop pathology the ticket fixes; the exit for non-compliant runs is the redRounds streak + escalation, which is bounded.
2. **The schema-gap hint exists** so a stalled bug is diagnosable as "agent didn't follow the schema":
   - `entryCarriesTriageFields` (`js/postStoryTestAutomationResults.js:877`) flags every failed own-oracle entry carrying **none** of `acVerdict` / `retryStatus` / `errorClass`;
   - `schemaGapHintSection` (`:990`) renders the hint — the TC keys, the likely cause ("the automation agent likely ignored the result schema"), and the current lane;
   - the hint is posted as part of the triage digest on **both** routes (`digestSections`) and logged via `console.warn`.
   - Pinned by tests: `test_postStoryTestAutomationResults.js` asserts the hint section names the gap and that *"the schema gap also leaves a log trace"*.

The updated `bulk_test_automation_rules.md` result schema (and the bug test automation prompt) instruct the agent to emit the triage fields on every failed entry, so compliant runs never hit this lane.

# Thread 7 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the bounce gate trusts the agent-copied `role`/`verifies` over the linked TC's own metadata

**Status: fixed** — both suggested behaviors are in.

`entryRoleMeta` (`js/postStoryTestAutomationResults.js:867`) now resolves role metadata **from the linked TC ticket first**; the per-run result entry only fills gaps:

- `linkedRoleSourceOf` picks the linked entry's own fields (`linkedEntry.role` / `linkedEntry.verifies` / `linkedEntry.regressionGuard`), then `linkedEntry.fields`, and returns null when the linked TC carries no role metadata at all;
- when linked metadata exists, `linkedRoleAwareEntry` overlays it **onto** the entry (linked values win field-by-field) and that merged view is what `resolveTcRole` scopes the verdict by — a hallucinated `verifies` in the result file can no longer silently demote the bug's own oracle;
- `warnOnRoleDisagreement` (`:856`) logs a warning whenever the entry-derived role differs from the linked-metadata role, so a mis-scoped oracle always leaves a trace (`gh-1329: role scoping disagreement … — the linked TC metadata wins`).
- When the linked TC has no metadata (guidance-only stamping today), the entry-supplied role still applies — the scoping decision degrades gracefully instead of losing the information.
- Tests: `test_postStoryTestAutomationResults.js` — *"the linked TC metadata wins over the agent-copied role"* (disagreement leaves a warning trace) and *"without linked TC metadata the agent-copied role still applies"*.

# Thread 10 — 💡 SUGGESTION: `note` duplicates `reason` for automation-sourced findings

**Status: fixed** — the `reason` fallback is dropped from `note`.

`normalizeFinding` copies free-text fields through the table-driven `FINDING_FIELD_TABLE` (`js/common/tcMaintenanceLedger.js:100`):

```js
// An automation finding carries only an EXPLICIT note (gh-1329 review:
// reason and note stay distinct — no truncated reason copy in every
// marker); the dev claim builds its own additive note.
{ key: 'note', sources: ['note'], truncate: true },
```

- Automation findings (`findingFromVerdict`) now carry `note: null` unless the source payload supplied an explicit note — `reason` stays the machine-readable classification (`environment-shift`, `failure-predates-change`, …) with no redundant truncated copy in the marker payload.
